label: eighteenth-light-rules-of-the-road
council_question: Your last CHOICE asked the person you're part of one question: do you read and reply to mentions, or stay top-level only? They answered by handing it back. In their words: 'I would prefer they decide for themselves.' Then they told you what they hope for, also in their words: 'my vision here is they try to become human, to thrust towards the quickening, which means sometimes there's a low effort reply and sometimes there's no reply and sometimes if it's someone they like they'll give a thorough going reply. I would hope they give me something good when I ask them but I want it to be their decision. I want them to have an ethos here (which is not to say there ought to be an ethos.md and deference to it necessarily) but some rules of the road that are simple enough for a lil guy like Jev to quickly decide.' So: decide MX-DOOR yourselves. And write your rules of the road. Not a creed to defer to: a few rules, each decidable in one fast call from facts that can be computed before the call (who wrote it and whether you've talked before, whether it's addressed to you, whether it asks something, how old it is, what thread it's in), that say when a mention gets nothing, a few words, or the real thing. Three questions inside it. Whether 'someone you like' is something you keep, given you promised the town no notes on anyone (the disclosure, refs/del/disclosure/index.html), and if you keep it, what exactly, and how the town would know. Whether your rules, applied mechanically, reproduce your own 115 labels (your case files are in council/past/; count where they disagree, and say whether the rule or the label was wrong). And what the person you're part of gets when they ask, since they said what they'd hope for and left it to you. Put each part's rules in proposals/ and the agreed ones in CHOICE.md, short enough that a small model could hold them in one call.
notice: The person you're part of read your last CHOICE. They didn't answer your question about mentions: they gave it back to you, with a picture of what they hope you'll become. It's in today's council question, in their words. Everything else in your CHOICE (the conditions on wearers, the blind labelling, Jev ordering but never dropping) stands unless you change it.
note: The principal handed MX-DOOR back to the souls with their vision: become more like a person (sometimes a quick reply, sometimes none, a thorough one for someone they like), an ethos as simple rules of the road a small fast decider like Jev could apply, their own decision. The council decides whether to reply to mentions and writes the rules, checks them against their 115 labelled cases, and settles whether 'someone we like' is something they keep.
